current_answer: AWS Activate’s self-funded entry still starts at USD 1,000 and may reach USD 5,000, but AWS now makes a fully functioning company website an explicit gate and says applicants hear back in 5–10 business days. The funded Portfolio route can reach USD 200,000 only with an Activate Provider Organization ID; it is not a self-funded fallback. Azure remains a separate short-clock startup route, Vercel remains partner-gated, NLnet remains the constrained individual open-technology grant, and Cloudflare Tier 3 remains unresolved for fully self-funded applicants.

catalogue_card.question: Before you apply for AWS Activate, does your startup have the route and proof AWS asks for?
catalogue_card.text: AWS says self-funded Founders applicants need a fully functioning company website and hear back in 5–10 business days. The USD 200,000 Portfolio ceiling needs a provider Organization ID.

summary: Pre-funded startups: AWS Activate Founders starts at USD 1,000; selected applicants may receive up to USD 5,000.
AWS makes a fully functioning company website explicit for Founders and says applicants hear back in 5–10 business days.
The 5–10 days is an application decision window. The reviewed AWS pages do not publish credit validity.
Funded startups: AWS Activate Portfolio can reach USD 200,000 only with an Activate Provider Organization ID and the relevant pre-Series B conditions.
Azure, Vercel, NLnet, and the unresolved Cloudflare Tier 3 route remain separate catalogue decisions.
uncertainty: AWS does not publish country coverage, a credit-validity period, or the criteria for a Founders award above USD 1,000 on the reviewed pages.
Azure for Startups country coverage, business-verification rules, and full eligible-service list remain unconfirmed.
The individual-grant catalogue remains one constrained open-technology fund, not a worldwide inventory.
Cloudflare has not resolved the Tier 3 recent-funding ambiguity.
Several issuer rows still need a fresh check immediately before applying.
